note: Codes: data/mexico_2025_safety.do (Bookmark #1, Q1 2025 Public Safety Perception) keeps the 59 INEGI columns bp1_1..bp1_9_6 from conjunto_de_datos_ensu_cb_0325.csv (import delimited case(lower)), with id = _n in file order, and reshapes long with item = column name (core model s3 pattern 1, no positional step). mapping_basis=data_labels: INEGI's 2025 Q1 data dictionary labels every BP1_* column (e.g. BP1_2_08 'Percepcion de seguridad en el cajero automatico localizado en la via publica'; BP1_5_4 'Cambiar sus habitos respecto a permitir que los (las) menores de edad que viven en el hogar salgan solos(as) por temor a sufrir algun delito'; BP1_6_12 '...: No lo hace'; BP1_9_5 'Percepcion del grado de confianza en la Fuerza Aerea Mexicana'); 59/59 labels agree in content with the questionnaire sub-item/option carrying the same number, and 144/144 shipped option_text values are character-identical to the catalogos/<item>.csv label for that code. Step 3b, 2025 Q1 vs 2024 (checked against the 2025 Q1 print, 2025 Q1 dictionary, catalogos, raw columns and .do, not assumed): 2025 Q1 Section I is the Q1/Q3 form -- 1.6 is the 14-indicator news-source checklist (bp1_6_01..13, 99; 0/1), NOT Q2/Q4's household-victimization bp1_6_1..8 -- and it matches 2024 Q1 (batch_675) except one sub-item: 1.5 item 4 (bp1_5_4) carries the Q3/Q4 2024 rewording 'permitir que los (las) menores de edad que viven en el hogar salgan solos(as)?' in place of 2024 Q1's 'permitir que salgan de su vivienda sus hijos(as) menores?' (print and dictionary both changed). Dictionary diff 0324 vs 0325 over the 59 BP1 variables: only BP1_5_4 (above) and the BP1_6_01/02 labels (now 'vecinos(as) o conocidos(as)', 'companeros(as)'), whose printed options already read that way in 2024 Q1 -- no change to shipped text; all 59 catalogos/bp1_*.csv byte-identical after line-ending normalisation. Print-level: the 2024 Q1 direction 'EL CODIGO 3 NO APLICA SOLO SE ACEPTA PARA LA POLICIA PREVENTIVA MUNICIPAL' is absent from 2025 Q1 1.7 (stripped anyway); the '[CDMX (3)]' row label is still printed and kept on bp1_7_1. Words: text_source=study_materials, the administered 2025 Q1 questionnaire wording (not the terser dictionary labels): 74 of the 75 distinct Spanish strings shipped are exact substrings of pdftotext -raw output of pp.2-3 after whitespace normalisation (unlike the 2024 Q1 PDF, the 2025 text layer carries the 1.7-1.9 stems and 1.9 options), and 110-dpi renders of pp.2-3 were read to confirm; the 75th, 'No se declaro como opcion afirmativa' (bp1_6_* code 0), is INEGI's catalogo value label, not questionnaire text, as in batch_675. Structure and conventions identical to batch_675: CP1 read-aloud intro in instructions; one section_id per question 1.1-1.9; for 1.2 and 1.4-1.9 the stem is in section_prompt and the sub-item/row in item_text; 1.1 and 1.3 are single items with the stem in item_text. Kept as printed: '(LUGAR)', '(CIUDAD)', '(AUTORIDAD)', 'la (al)', 'la (del)', 'la (el)' fills; '(a)'/'(as)' gender fills; trailing '?' and '...'; 1.1/1.3 options with trailing '?'; 'No sabe/ no responde' spacing on 1.6 code 99; 'Otro'/'Otra' write-in rows as the bare word. Normalised: line wraps joined; double spaces collapsed (1.6 opt 01 'conocidos(as)  en'). Stripped: question/option numbers, dot leaders, entry boxes, blank write-in lines, 'ESPECIFIQUE', interviewer directions (CIRCULE UN SOLO CODIGO; REGISTRE EL CODIGO CORRESPONDIENTE A CADA OPCION; MUESTRE LA TARJETA 'A' Y CIRCULE LOS CODIGOS CORRESPONDIENTES; PASA AL SIGUIENTE RENGLON; the 1.8/1.9 skip note). Options: only levels present in the live data get rows (no row for 3 'No aplica' / 9 'No sabe / no responde', set missing by the .do); every level each item's respondents used has an option row (144/144 live item x level cells). Cross-check (route 9 style, .cache/mexico_2025_q1safety_perception/counts.py vs live_counts.csv from a server-side GROUP BY item,resp query; no export): RESPONSE-DATA DEFECT -- the live table has exactly 1,048,575 rows (the 2^20-1 spreadsheet row limit) over 19,980 ids, while the raw 2025 Q1 file has 23,591 respondents and the .do's long output should have 1,240,696 rows. Live = the first 1,048,575 rows of the .do's output sorted by id,item: 142/144 item x level counts are identical to raw rows 1..19980 after the .do's recodes (e.g. bp1_1 1/2 = 8135/11785, bp1_3 1..4 = 5533/3616/5953/4614, bp1_6_01 0/1 = 8430/11550, bp1_5_4 1/2 = 6131/8920, bp1_9_1 1..4 = 969/5443/3472/2621), and the other 2 are id 19980's last two sorted rows (bp1_9_3 = 3 and bp1_9_4 = 3: raw 2425/1687, live 2424/1686). Respondents 19981..23591 (3,611) and 192,121 long rows are absent. Against the full raw file all 144 cells differ (e.g. bp1_1 1/2 full = 9543/13983). Item set and resp set unaffected, so the item text is correct for what is live. Dictionary defects: Reference names 'ENSU 2023' while data and wording are the 2025 Q1 wave (file suffix 0325) -- same as the siblings. English in _translated is this project's own translation (machine_translation): reused verbatim from batch_675 (2024 Q1) for every string whose Spanish is identical, and from batch_688 (2024 Q4) for bp1_5_4 ('allowing minors who live in the household to go out alone?', Spanish identical to 688's); nothing translated fresh. INEGI publishes no English questionnaire.
public_note: Fuente: INEGI, Encuesta Nacional de Seguridad Pública Urbana (ENSU) 2025, primer trimestre -- IRW transcribed Section I (questions 1.1-1.9) from INEGI's questionnaire, stripped interviewer directions, took the 0/1 labels for the question 1.6 information-source indicators (including its 'No sabe/ no responde' and 'Otra' indicators, which are shipped as items) from INEGI's data catalogue, and added an English translation of its own; INEGI does not endorse this item text.
